newsitem.title: USA: 3Com says revenue growth may trail industry.
newsitem.headline: 3Com says revenue growth may trail industry.

text.p: 3Com Corp said in its quarterly report that it could see slower revenue increases than the rest of the networking industry because of falling prices and weaker demand for computer networking gear.

3Com, the second-biggest networking equipment maker after Cisco Systems Inc, is facing increasing pressure as Intel Corp makes more low-priced networking equipment for PCs and as Cisco expands its lead in gear for high-end networks.
In addition, most companies have completed building their computer networks, and are buying less gear.

"Based on recent softening of demand for networking products and competitive pricing pressures, 3Com anticipates that its results may fall below (the 30-50 percent revenue growth rate of the rest of the industry) in coming quarters," the company revealed in its 10Q filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
In its fiscal third quarter ended February 28, revenue rose 28 percent to $786.8 million. In previous quarters, the revenue increases were at least 40 percent.
